summary.text: Adam Bremner is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a teacher and union member, and a lead organiser of the No Sunbury Waste Incinerator campaign, which is fighting a waste incinerator proposed for the area. He says public schools in the outer west are underfunded and that local services have been neglected.

priorities.text: Better funding and conditions for public schools
Stopping the proposed Sunbury waste incinerator
Taking on big polluters over environmental pollution
Renewing community houses, schools, sports centres, hospitals and roads in the outer west
We need a system for us, and to put people before profit.

sources.title: Sunbury: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Adam Bremner, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Elmer Batres is the Family First candidate for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he was born in El Salvador, grew up during its civil war and came to Australia with his family in 1990. An ordained Baptist pastor who has led churches in West Footscray, Kerang and Port Campbell, he now works as a prison chaplain.

summary.text: Geoff Vine is The West Party's candidate for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. On his party page he says he built a home in the area in 1983, has led a service club and oversees a local business, Vine Distribution. He says he is standing because he believes the major parties have let the area down.

summary.text: Josh Bull has been the Labor MP for Sunbury since the seat was first contested in 2014, and was re-elected in 2018 and 2022. Born in Sunbury, he trained and worked as a teacher and was later a staffer for state and federal Labor MPs. He has been a parliamentary secretary since 2018 and currently assists the Treasurer and covers roads. He is recontesting Sunbury in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Level Crossing Removals
Parliamentary Secretary for Carers and Volunteers
Chief of staff to Rob Mitchell, federal member for McEwen
Electorate officer for Liz Beattie, member for Yuroke

priorities.text: Equality, fairness and social justice
High-quality education
Better health and transport services

summary.text: Lauren Granger-Brown is the Greens candidate for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian election. She has spent more than twenty years in education, chiefly teaching English to migrants and refugees, and has also tutored students heading to university and trained other teachers. Originally from Melbourne, she twice ran for the Greens at Queensland state elections, in Gympie in 2020 and in Maryborough in 2024.

occupation.text: Teacher of English to migrants and refugees

priorities.text: Affordable housing and relief from everyday costs such as groceries
Free and frequent public transport
Climate action, with no new coal and gas
Keeping AI data centres out of residential neighbourhoods
Stronger protection for nature

summary.text: Rohanna Mohr is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. summary.text: Simmone Cottom is the Liberal candidate for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian election. She was born in Sunbury, went to Salesian College in the town and works as a senior tax consultant. She ran for the Liberals in Sunbury at the 2022 state election and in the federal seat of Hawke in 2025, losing both times.

priorities.text: Reducing crime
Lowering the cost of living
Better access to mental health support

summary.text: Steve Jack Medcraft, who appears in the ABC's guide as Steve "Jack" Medcraft, is standing as an independent for Sunbury at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The ABC gives no biography. Wikipedia records a Jack Medcraft as a Hume City councillor and deputy mayor before 2024, and a Steve Medcraft as an independent candidate at three earlier state elections, including Sunbury in 2014, but no source confirms either is this candidate.
